ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, individual and corporate beneficial owners holding 25% or more, authorized signatories, and any related-party counterparties against (i) the United Nations Consolidated List, (ii) the OFAC SDN List and applicable OFAC sectoral/non-SDN sanctions where USD payment rails are used, (iii) the consolidated sanctions lists administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and (iv) Quebec/Canadian criminal and administrative enforcement records. FINTRAC guidance defines politically exposed persons (PEPs) as individuals holding prominent public functions, and enhanced due diligence must be applied to any domestic or foreign PEP. Given the Low_Risk_Standard classification of an omni-helpdesk SaaS business, a logical risk assessment should still document source of funds for contributions in kind, verify the general partner's financial position, and replicate screening at least annually or upon admission of any new limited partner.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Online Filing Services (Services en ligne du Registraire des entreprises)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the Charter of the French Language, the legal name of a Quebec-domiciled limited partnership must be in French or must have a French generic designation, generally as 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'. A non-French name is only acceptable when accompanied by a French legal designation or where a recognized exception applies (e.g., a proper name or a name used exclusively outside Quebec). Names must use the Latin alphabet; transliteration of non-Latin characters into French/Latin script is permissible, but the registered name must be legible and consistent with the French-language doctrine of Quebec.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada / Québec (where the name suggests official government sponsorship)
Coopérative / Cooperative (limited by law to cooperative structures)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is refused, the applicant or agent must first request an administrative review (demande de révision) before the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the refusal notification. The request must include a name analysis memorandum addressing the statutory prohibition grounds, a proposed French legal designation, evidence of the requested legal form (S.E.C.), and, where relevant, consent letters for sensitive terms. If the administrative review is dismissed, judicial recourse lies before the Court of Quebec in accordance with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and its regulation. A name reservation may be renewed by filing a new request before the original validity window expires; no automatic extension exists after the 90-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A commercial address for service in Quebec is mandatory for the limited partnership. A managed virtual office with a physical location, human reception, open mail handling, and access to books and records may be acceptable for a low-risk SaaS/helpdesk entity. A mail-drop-only or unstaffed virtual address generally does not satisfy the REQ address-for-service requirements and may be treated as non-compliant commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-negligible - approximately 5-10% probability of an unannounced on-site verification during the first 12 months of operation, particularly if the registered office is a virtual office provider or if the REQ/AMF conducts a general compliance sweep. The likelihood rises to approximately 15-20% where the corporate general partner has a prior administrative compliance history or where a beneficial owner is a foreign PEP or high-risk tax resident.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada) via the My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Provincial (Quebec): Revenu Québec via the CLIC portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/). The Quebec Limited Partnership (CA_LP) is a distinct 'person' for GST/HST and QST purposes and requires a federal Business Number (BN) and a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) File the Limited Partnership declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the NEQ; the LP is constituted under Book IV of the Civil Code of Quebec. 2) Apply to the CRA for a 9-digit Business Number using Form RC1 ('Request for a Business Number') or the Business Registration Online (BRO) service, selecting GST/HST, payroll, and deemed import/export accounts as applicable; the LP is registered in its own name, not in the partners' names. 3) Once registered federally, complete the single-window enterprise registration with Revenu Québec to activate the QST account, which is mandatory when taxable supplies in Quebec exceed CAD 30,000 or when the business is in a no-threshold sector (none applicable to helpdesk SaaS). 4) For a non-resident limited partner, file CRA Form RC3 (Application for Authorization of a Tax Representative) and confirm compliance with Part XIII non-resident withholding on Canadian-source allocated income; for QST, non-resident partners are deemed to carry on the partnership's Quebec business. 5) Activate the CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec CLIC credentials, appoint an authorized representative/filer, and register for electronic GST/HST and QST return filing (mandatory for registrants reporting electronically by default).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. Under Income Tax Act s.96, a Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax: no entity-level federal or Quebec income tax; each partner is taxed on its allocated share of partnership income/loss, and non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII withholding on Canadian-source partnership income. For GST/HST and QST, however, the Excise Tax Act and Quebec Sales Tax Act deem the partnership to be a person, so the LP holds its own GST/HST and QST registrations and must collect/remit tax on taxable supplies. The commercial model (helpdesk SaaS, low AML risk, no statutory license) does not alter this default classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no U.S.-style 'check-the-box' election. Relevant elections and hybrid-mismatch mechanisms for a Quebec LP: (i) ITA s.96 designation of each partner's income/loss allocation in the partnership agreement, binding unless CRA considers it artificial; (ii) ETA s.209(6) election to voluntarily register as a GST/HST registrant while below the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold (reverse is not permitted once over the threshold); (iii) ETA s.191 election for supplies among closely related corporations (largely unavailable to an LP unless 90% corporate control exists within the group); (iv) ETA s.211 election for exempt financial services (not applicable to helpdesk SaaS); (v) ITA s.215(2) and s.216(4) elections enabling a non-resident partner to have withholding tax remitted on a net basis or deemed-paid basis; (vi) hybrid mismatch alignment rules (ITA ss.18.2, 18.21, the EIFEL regime effective for taxation years beginning on or after October 1, 2023) mandate an interest-deduction cap for large groups and are mandatory, not elective. No specific Quebec pass-through or transparency election exists beyond the default statutory treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT system: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (5% in Quebec, which does not apply the HST) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) under the Quebec Sales Tax Act (9.98%), administered respectively by the CRA and Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. The GST/HST small-supplier threshold (ETA s.148(3)) is based on worldwide taxable supplies (including supplies by associated persons) over the preceding four calendar quarters and any current quarter; the QST small-supplier threshold (Quebec Sales Tax Act s.85) is likewise CAD 30,000. Once the CA_LP's taxable helpdesk SaaS revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 in any qualifying four-quarter window, GST/HST and QST registration becomes mandatory; voluntary registration is available below the threshold and is often elected to claim input tax credits on startup costs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no pre-stamped digital tax invoice, and no per-transaction API authorization exists in Canada or Quebec for B2B/B2C invoices. Mandates applicable to the CA_LP: (i) electronic filing of GST/HST returns through CRA GST/HST NETFILE (GST34 form) and electronic remittance for registrants above CRA thresholds; (ii) electronic filing of QST returns through Revenu Québec's CLIC/EBusiness services for registrants required to report electronically; (iii) adoption of the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Standard (PEPPOL BIS 3.0) is mandatory for suppliers to the federal government (B2G) from fiscal years 2026-2027 onward for large taxpayers, but remains voluntary for commercial invoices issued to Stripe Billing / PayPal customers. The CA_LP must nevertheless maintain compliant transaction records and invoice fields required by CRA and Revenu Québec (seller identity, BN/QST numbers, tax rates, and amounts).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Quebec LP supplying multi-channel helpdesk, customer-support, and conversational-bot cloud services (ISIC 6201) may zero-rate its supplies under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.7 (services supplied to non-residents) if all of the following apply: (a) the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered under Part IX of the ETA at the time the supply is made; (b) the service is not performed wholly or substantially in Canada (remote helpdesk delivery via cloud infrastructure and offshore support agents satisfies this); (c) the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situate in Canada; and (d) the supply is not for consumption, use, or enjoyment in Canada by a GST/HST registrant. Equivalent zero-rating applies for QST under the Quebec Sales Tax Act s.14 and s.9, with the recipient required to be a 'non-designated consumer' or non-resident who is not a QST registrant. If the helpdesk services support Canadian-based clients or Canadian go-to-market SaaS subscriptions, the supply is taxable at the combined 14.98% rate; reverse-charge self-assessment obligations may apply to non-resident recipients in limited circumstances.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) and Canadian International Trade Single Window export reporting, required for tangible goods and applied analogously where digital deliverables are embedded in the transaction
Commercial invoice bearing the supplier's BN and QST registration numbers, with an express zero-rated classification and reference to ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.7 / QST Act equivalent
Signed Master Services Agreement, statement of work, and helpdesk service logs demonstrating offshore performance, non-resident recipient identity, and foreign place of use
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill, where any physical components (e.g., hardware or SDK media) accompany the SaaS/helpdesk supply, as supplementary export proof
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment confirmations or banking records showing receipt of overseas client consideration in the CA_LP's Canadian account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada and Quebec do not codify a statutory 180-day exchange-repatriation deadline; however, the CRA and Revenu Québec require exporters to substantiate zero-rating on an ongoing basis, and a 180-day benchmark is the practical audit-evidence horizon for matching export declarations to inward remittances. Penalties for fraudulent zero-rating claims: (i) federal Excise Tax Act s.280(1) imposes a penalty of CAD 5,000 or 25% of the net tax sought to be avoided, whichever is greater, for false statements or omissions; (ii) ETA s.239 creates criminal liability (fine up to 25% of the deficiency plus imprisonment for up to 5 years) for willful evasion with intent to deceive; (iii) CRA can reassess retroactively for up to four years plus a 12-year window where misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, or willful default (ETR s.298); (iv) Revenu Québec under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c. A-6.002) s.1033.1 imposes penalties of CAD 5,000 to CAD 25,000 plus 50% of the amount evaded for deliberate false statements, and s.1032(1) penalizes failure to register or file QST; (v) QST clawbacks require repayment of the full QST not collected, plus interest from the original supply date and compounding penalties; (vi) joint and several liability may extend to general partners who knowingly participate in a false zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary and payments-system authority; OSFI as prudential banking supervisor; FINTRAC as AML/ATF supervisory agency; Department of Finance Canada for sanctions and financial policy; and the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) of Quebec as the provincial money-services-business regulator. Canada has no dedicated SAFE-style foreign-exchange control agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII; CAD is freely floating with no exchange-control permission requirements. Profit remittance for the Quebec LP is constrained only by taxation: distributions of partnership income to non-resident limited partners attract Part XIII withholding under subsection 212(1) of the Income Tax Act (default 25%, reduced by double-tax treaties, e.g., Canada-US treaty rates of 5-15%), and the LP must file T5013 and NR4 returns and maintain CRS/FATCA partner self-certification. The remaining commercial hurdle is bank KYC documentation proving source of funds rather than any FX quota.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, no statutory timeline, and no requirement to sell export or SaaS receipts into CAD; receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts at domestic banks. The only applicable reporting requirements are FINTRAC's mandatory reporting of international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, CRS/FATCA foreign-account reporting, and Quebec and Canada tax disclosure obligations. No conversion is compelled at any threshold.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a receivable collection gateway; Low as a primary liquidity-clearing rail. Wise (FINTRAC-registered MSB) and PayPal Business (authorized MSB) can lawfully collect Stripe/B2B helpdesk fees and sweep into the Tier-1 operational account; Airwallex may be used for supplier payout automation if registered with FINTRAC. Legal constraints: (i) an offshore EMI or payment service provider that is not FINTRAC-registered cannot lawfully provide money-services-business services in or from Canada; (ii) in Quebec, money-services-business activity is further subject to the Money-Services Businesses Act and AMF registration or exemption; (iii) using unregistered offshore EMIs as the main treasury account may trigger aggravated FINTRAC EDD, destabilize the partnership capital-account mapping, and create non-Canadian functional-currency exposure under subsection 261(1) of the Income Tax Act. Recommended posture: EMI as a pass-through with daily sweeps only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in-branch or equivalent notarized interview in the majority of cases: the authorized executive of the corporate general partner and every individual limited partner with 25% or greater ownership must be identified via interactive KYC. Banks with Quebec operations (National Bank, Desjardins, BMO, Laurentian) generally require a physical visit from the general partner; RBC and TD permit a hybrid remote open for low-risk, fully Canadian-resident structures using video call plus notarized attestation by a Quebec lawyer or notary. A fully remote opening is not available where the LP has non-resident partners at the 25%+ threshold, where the general partner is offshore, or where the beneficial-ownership chain is multi-jurisdictional. Practical mandate: one physical KYC visit by the general partner in Montreal or Quebec City with passport, LP agreement, source-of-wealth, and corporate registrations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed limited-partner beneficiaries: LP register shows only the general partner while side letters allocate 25%+ beneficial interests to silent partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership waterfall: executed LP agreement with no-oral-modification clause, Registraire des entreprises du Québec LP certificate, partners' capital account ledger, 25%+ beneficial-owner identification declarations (name, DOB, residence, tax ID) with valid picture identification, and CRS/FATCA self-certification for every partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore or zero-tax resident general partner or limited partners controlling the Quebec LP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substantive Canadian nexus file: 12-month Quebec registered-office lease, payroll and source-deduction evidence (RPC/QPIP), T5013 filing history, bank references for each offshore partner, source-of-wealth declaration, OFAC/PEP/UN sanctions screen results, and Canadian tax counsel residency analysis of the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue concentrated in third-party processors (Stripe/PayPal) with elevated chargeback ratios and unclear end-customer nature.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 15-month merchant settlement history, platform KYC documents, end-customer helpdesk contracts and invoices, published product and application URL, service-level agreement, refund policy, chargeback rate below 0.75%, and order-to-bank reconciliation workbook.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contributions sourced through cryptocurrency exchanges or non-bank intermediaries rather than regulated banking channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-call notices issued under the LP agreement, fiat bank settlement statements, signed no-crypto attestation by all partners, chain-analysis report if any crypto touch-point exists, exchange transfer statements, and confirmation that final funding originates from a regulated OECD banking system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-sensitive commercial exposure: helpdesk bot infrastructure or customer subprocessors in embargoed jurisdictions (Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, DPRK) or OFAC-blocked regions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 6201 scope and customer-jurisdiction memo, automated weekly OFAC/OFSI/EU screening logs, customer geolocation/IP evidence, no-export clause in the master service agreement, controlled-goods or dual-use declaration where applicable, and export-control counsel certification of compliance with the Special Economic Measures Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) route all partner capital as SWIFT MT103 with SWIFT gpi, using ISO 20022 Purpose Code CAPCONT in field 77B and a clear remittance reference to the capital call under the LP agreement; (2) incoming CAD settles via Payments Canada Lynx; incoming USD clears via Fedwire or CHIPS into the bank's U.S. correspondent and is then internally converted to CAD only when operating liquidity demands; euro capital injections utilize TARGET2 and SEPA; (3) any international EFT of CAD 10,000 or more is FINTRAC-reportable and will trigger full source-of-funds verification; the LP must keep ready the capital call, partner subscription agreement and source-of-wealth file; (4) capital proceeds must be allocated to segregated partner capital sub-accounts and never commingled with operating cash in order to preserve the limited-partner capital accounts under the Civil Code of Quebec and the LP agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail hierarchy: (1) domestic CAD disbursements via Payments Canada Lynx (high-value) with pre-authorized debits for recurring payroll; (2) cross-border SWIFT MT103 STP with MT202 cover for cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), SaaS vendor payments and international recruitment; (3) USD settlements through RBC, TD or BMO U.S. correspondent banks (Fedwire/CHIPS) for US subcontractors; (4) euro-denominated disbursements via SEPA Credit Transfer through an EU-domiciled treasury sub-account; (5) commercial letters of credit (UCP600) are contractually available from Canadian banks but are economically inappropriate for intangible helpdesk services and should be reserved for physical telephony or data-centre hardware imports, with EDC mitigation. All outbound EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC reporting; maintain a treasury-approved beneficiary whitelist with bank account confirmation and sanctions pre-screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CAD foreign-exchange forward contracts (maximum maturity 12 months, non-speculative, documentation under ISDA 2002 with CORRA as fallback reference rate)
FX swaps for efficient short-term USD/CAD cash conversion with clean master-agreement collateral in the Canadian repo market
Cross-currency swaps converting USD SaaS annual recurring revenue into CAD floating cash flows, hedge-accounted under IFRS 9 and supported by ISDA schedule
OTC vanilla USD/CAD options used solely to protect committed foreign-currency operating disbursements, with premium paid in freely convertible CAD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, TRY) to hedge subcontractor cost centres; NDFs are not applicable to CAD because CAD is fully deliverable
Standardized USD/CAD futures and options listed on the Montreal Exchange (TMX Group) as margin-efficient exchange-traded hedges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days after the enterprise registration anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the enterprise and its partners to monetary penalties under the Legal Publicity Act; continued failure for three consecutive years triggers administrative cancellation or radiation from the Quebec enterprise register, ending the partnership's registration rights in Quebec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than March 31 following the calendar year in which the partnership's fiscal period ends; other deadlines apply for non-calendar fiscal periods under the prescribed T5013 rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a complete partnership information return may result in CRA-administered late-filing penalties, daily penalty assessments for continued default, interest, and criminal prosecution for deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the prescribed due date under the Taxation Act for partnership information returns; for a December 31 fiscal period-end, generally the same calendar deadline as the federal T5013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or incomplete filing can trigger interest, penalties, and administrative sanctions by Revenu Québec, including recovery measures and fines for failure to supply required information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec-registered limited partnership by the Legal Publicity Act or Civil Code of Québec; an audit may become compulsory when required by the limited partnership agreement, securities law filings, financial institution covenants, or investor rights agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private partnerships; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for public or securities-reporting entities, both under the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general Canadian and Quebec corporate rate (15% Federal Part I after abatement and general rate reduction; 11.5% Quebec). The Quebec Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent: the LP itself pays no income tax; each partner pays at their applicable federal and Quebec rates on the allocated share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for CCPC partners); Quebec reduced corporate rate of 3.2% for the same active business income; Federal SR&ED investment tax credit 35% (CCPC) / 15% (non-CCPC); Quebec CIRI R&D credit 14%-30%; Quebec refundable multimedia product design credit (CCPI) up to 37.5% (enhanced to 52.5% for small businesses); Federal Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit 15%-17.5% for qualifying helpdesk/cloud products.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013-SUM (Summary) and individual T5013 slips (Statement of Partnership Income) transmitted electronically via CRA Internet File Transfer (XML schema) or CRA-certified third-party software (e.g., Intuit Profile, DT Professional Suite).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The partnership information return must be filed within 5 months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period (CRA Guide RC4393). No automatic extension is available for T5013 filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross business revenue of the helpdesk/cloud subscription activity before any deduction, reconciled to the billing pipeline (Stripe, PayPal) and deferred revenue schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source gross revenue; the non-resident partner's share is tracked for Part XIII withholding exposure and treaty allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income after deductible expenses: hosting, employee compensation, software licensing, marketing, professional fees, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This allocable net figure determines the non-resident partner's Canadian-source business income under ITA s. 253 and the related Part XIII liability under s. 212(2.3).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 (Net Partnership Income / Loss for Income Tax Purposes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate income available for allocation to partners after all income tax adjustments, including capital cost allowance, reserves, and partnership-level elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allocation percentage in the LP agreement governs each non-resident partner's T5013 slip amount; any inconsistent allocation invites reassessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner-by-partner allocation of income, losses, charitable donations, and non-deductible items in accordance with the limited partnership agreement and any mid-year transfer of interests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each non-resident partner must receive a slip; treaty relief is claimed only on the properly allocated share, and withholding on distributions is computed on the same share.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty for T5013: CAD 25.00 per day per slip, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; gross negligence penalty up to CAD 7,500 per slip. Failure to file T106 (non-arm's-length non-resident transactions) attracts CAD 100.00 per day, minimum CAD 1,000 and maximum CAD 25,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: CO-17 (Declaration de renseignements d'une societe de personnes / Partnership Information Return) and Releve 15 (Amounts Paid to a Non-Resident), filed electronically via Revenu Quebec's Online Services (EDEN portal) or approved commercial software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period (Quebec Taxation Act s. 1030). Electronic filing is mandatory for partnership returns above Revenu Quebec's volume threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, NEQ (Registraire des entreprises number), registered office in Quebec, fiscal period start and end dates, and general partner identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare each non-resident partner's country of residence and treaty status; identify the general partner responsible for withholding and remitting provincial amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-source gross revenue and deductible operating expenses for the helpdesk business, including reconciliation to the federal T5013 income and capital cost allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Quebec-source income is allocated to non-resident partners; the allocable share is reported on Releve 15 for provincial withholding purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distributive share of income or loss, tax credits, and adjusted cost base information allocated to each partner under the LP agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full legal name, address, and tax identification numbers of non-resident partners; allocate using the same percentages as the federal T5013 to avoid cross-return mismatches.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late CO-17 penalty: CAD 25.00 per day late, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500. Where the omission facilitates Quebec tax evasion, additional civil penalties of up to 20% of evaded tax and non-deductible statutory interest may apply.
